### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

Hi! I'm a native Korean speaker and a researcher currently studying LLMs and inference/serving frameworks.

SGLang is gaining increasing interest among researchers and developers in Korea, and a few Korean researchers and I would like to contribute Korean translations to make the documentation more accessible to Korean users.
We thought the SGLang Cookbook would be a good place to start because its practical, model-specific guides are especially useful for users working with and deploying different models.

I noticed that multilingual documentation was previously discussed in #4155. Rather than proposing localization of the entire documentation at once, we would like to begin with a small number of Cookbook pages and gradually expand from there.


So before starting a PR, I wanted to ask:

- Would the project be open to accepting Korean translations of the Cookbook?
- Are there any plans to support additional languages in the documentation more broadly?
- Since I couldn't find an existing i18n structure, what structure or approach would the maintainers prefer for localized documentation?

If the project is open to this, we'd be happy to follow the maintainers' preferred approach.

### Related resources

- #4155 — Previous discussion on multilingual documentation
- SGLang Cookbook: https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/intro
title: [Feature] Korean Localization for SGLang Cookbook
